description: Core personal finance math for high school

cards.back: I = P * r * t where P is principal, r is annual rate, t is time in years.
A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) where n is compounds per year.
New = Original * (1 + rate). For 8% increase, multiply by 1.08.
New = Original * (1 - rate). For 15% discount, multiply by 0.85.
Tax or tip amount = price * rate. Total = price + add-ons.
Markup adds percent to cost. Markdown subtracts percent from listed price.
APR is nominal yearly rate. APY includes compounding and is effective annual yield.
Payment depends on principal, monthly rate, and number of payments. Longer term lowers payment but increases total interest.
DTI = monthly debt payments / gross monthly income. Lower DTI usually means lower risk.
Net cash flow = income - expenses. Positive flow builds savings.
Common target is 3-6 months of essential expenses.
Depreciation is value decrease over time. Linear model subtracts same amount each period.
Paying only minimum extends payoff time and greatly increases total interest paid.
Break-even occurs where revenue equals cost. Profit starts after this point.
Unit price = total cost / quantity. Compare unit prices for best value.
Real value adjusts for inflation; nominal value does not.
Approximate doubling time in years is 72 / annual percent rate.
